_about: The Help Center's built-in setup guides (helpdesk.js adds each once, and brings an unedited one up to date when this file changes; staff edit them on the site). Blocks: h, p, steps, img, video.

articles.title: Which apps does our church need?
articles.summary: Who uses which app, and where most churches start.

body.text: Central is a set of apps that find each other on your church's network. Most people only ever open one of them, the one that matches what they do on a Sunday. Here's who uses what.

items: **Central Pedal** is the box on the floor in front of the worship leader or the keys player. It plays your pads and multitracks, with the click and spoken cues, and shows the chart and the lyrics. You can plug a guitar or keyboard into it too. It comes from us built and ready to play.
**Central Pedal Control** is the same pedal app on your computer, tablet or phone. I use it at home to build the setlist and set up the songs, then send it all to the pedal with Upload.

**Central Control** is for whoever runs the desk. Lights, lyrics, slides, cameras, the stream, in-ears and the run sheet all live here. The person in charge of it is the main admin, and anyone helping is an admin.
**Central Usage** is for musicians and singers. It shows your own chart and the lyrics, plays your instrument sound, and gives you your own in-ear mix.
**Central Services** is the schedule. It shows who's serving, who's away and what's being played. Everyone in the church can have it.
**Central Production** is a free studio for making your own tracks, loops, pads, instruments and plugins.

body.text: If you're starting from nothing, I'd get a church pack. Lite, Regular, Plus and Ultra each come with the Central Control, Central Usage and Central Pedal Control keys for a team of that size, plus Central Services slots. Add the pedal if you want pads and tracks on the floor, and a sound plan if you want better sounds. Not sure which size? Pricing has a short "Which plan do I need?" helper.

articles.title: Setting up the Central Pedal
articles.summary: From the box to your first song. You'll need a phone and about fifteen minutes.

body.text: This is how I set up a new pedal. Have your phone with you and know your church's Wi-Fi password. It takes about fifteen minutes.
Plug it in

items: Plug in the power supply that came with the pedal. It starts by itself, and the 3.5" touch screen comes on after about 30 seconds.
Plug your headphones or the cable to the sound desk into the headphone jack. That's outputs 1 and 2. If your pedal has a DAC board, it's outputs 3 and 4, and a USB audio interface comes after that.
A monitor is optional. Plug it into HDMI 1. HDMI 2 can show the lyrics to the room.

body.text: Get it on your Wi-Fi

items: On your phone, join the Wi-Fi called "Central Pedal Setup". The setup page should open by itself. If it doesn't, go to http://10.42.0.1 in your phone's browser.
Pick your church's Wi-Fi and type its password. Choose the touch screen you have, and a 4-digit code. If your church uses Central Control, use the main admin's code.
Press Upload. The pedal joins your Wi-Fi, downloads the driver for your screen and restarts once. When it's back, Central Control and Central Pedal Control can find it.

body.alt: The Central Pedal's LIVE screen: the setlist on the left, the song's sections, PAUSE and NEXT in the middle, pads below

body.text: Check the sound

items: On the pedal, open Settings → Sound → Test sound and press 1, then 2. You should hear a tone in the left ear, then the right.
If you don't, the pedal tells you underneath where the sound stopped and fixes what it can. Press the output again to check.
If the headphone jack crackles and you can't hear the music, open Settings → Sound → Output device and set Headphone jack buffer to Biggest.

body.text: Your first setlist

The easiest way is Central Pedal Control on your computer. Press + Add songs and pick your own MP3s or WAVs, a multitrack, or something from Central Tracks. Put the songs in order, then press Upload. You can also add songs on the pedal itself from a USB stick, on the Tracks tab.
You don't need to update the pedal by hand. It checks every few hours and installs when nothing's playing. Settings → Software updates & backup shows what it's doing.

articles.title: The main admin's first hour
articles.summary: Make your church's account, install Central Control, hand out keys and give each computer its job.

body.text: You're the main admin, so you set things up for everyone else. Give yourself an hour and do these in order.

items: On this website, go to Account → Make an account and choose "Set up a new church". Use the church's own email address, not your personal one, because that account owns the keys. Then confirm the email we send you.
Buy a church pack from Pricing. The keys show up under Account → My products, and we email them to you as well.

Install Central Control on the computer at the desk. You'll find it under Downloads. The first time it opens, it asks for the church's name and a key, then which jobs this computer does: lyrics, lights, cameras, in-ears, tracks, the stream mix or slides.
When it asks for a 4-digit admin code, pick one and remember it. You'll need it later to change a computer's jobs.

Back on the website, open Account → Your church & team. Add your second main admin if you have one, then your admins (they use Central Control) and your musicians and singers (they use Central Usage). Each person gets an email with their key and a download link.
In Central Control, open the Devices tab. The pedal and the other computers on your network show up there, and you can change any computer's jobs from its Jobs menu.

body.alt: Central Control's Devices tab, with the pedal and the church's computers

body.text: A church can have two main admins. Main admins can change people, roles and billing. Admins run the service but can't change those things.

articles.title: Adding admins, musicians and singers
articles.summary: Give people their keys from the Teams page, and take a key back when someone moves on.

items: Sign in on this website as the church or as a main admin, and open Account → Your church & team.
Under Teams, add the person's name and email to the right list. Admins use Central Control, Users use Central Usage, and Pedal Control is for whoever gets the pedal ready.
They get an email with their key, a link to download their app and how to sign in. The key also shows under their own Account → My products.
When someone leaves, press Remove next to their name. Their key is free for the next person, and their app asks for a key the next time it checks.
Musicians can also join on their own with your church's code when they make an account. The code is on the same page.

body.text: A Central Usage key works on two devices, so a player can have the app at church and at home. A Central Control key is for one computer.

articles.title: For musicians and singers: Central Usage
articles.summary: Get your chart, the lyrics, your sound and your own in-ear mix.

body.text: Your church will have sent you an email with a key and a link. That's all you need.

items: Download Central Usage from the link in the email. It runs on Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone, iPad and Android.
Sign in with the email address your church used, or paste the key from the email.
Pick what you play. The chart follows whatever song the pedal is playing, in the key and clef you choose.
For in-ears, plug headphones into your device or your audio interface, and set your own mix of the tracks and the band.
To play through it, plug in your keyboard or guitar and pick a sound. A sound plan adds a lot more of them.

body.alt: Central Usage's chord chart following the song

articles.title: Connecting Planning Center and CCLI
articles.summary: Bring your plans in, put the copyright line on screen and let the CCLI report fill itself in.

body.text: Planning Center

items: As a main admin, open Account → Planning Center & CCLI on this website, or Settings → Planning Center & CCLI in Central Control, and press Connect Planning Center.
Sign in to Planning Center and allow Motion Audio Central. After that, every device in your church can see your upcoming plans.
Pick a plan to turn it into a setlist. Songs are matched to Central Tracks and your own songs by CCLI number first, then by title. Anything it can't find is listed, with how to get it.
It looks for changes to your plans every 15 minutes. If you've just changed something, press Check for changes.

body.text: Not connected yet? You can still import a plan from a file. Export the plan from Planning Center as a CSV, or use a plain list of songs.
CCLI

items: Type in your CCLI licence number and your streaming licence number on Account → Planning Center & CCLI.
In the song editor, import songs from SongSelect (.txt or .usr files) or ChordPro. The words, chords, writers, copyright and CCLI number all come in with the song.
The copyright line goes on the first slide of each song. You can move it to the last slide or every slide, and change how it's worded.
Whenever a song's words go up on a real screen, it's counted once for that day. The CCLI report on your Account page downloads in the layout CCLI's reporting page asks for.

articles.title: Lights: first steps
articles.summary: Build your stage, add your real lights and make your first scene.

body.text: You'll need Central Control on the computer that's connected to your DMX interface or Art-Net node.

items: In Central Control, open the Devices tab and give that computer the Lights job.
Open Lighting and press Build my stage. It asks how big your stage is, its shape, any risers and screens, the room and seats, and where your lights hang, then builds it all in 3D.

Add your real lights with Find a real light…. There are 2,272 fixtures to search by maker and model. Pick the mode, the universe and the address. If yours isn't there, Make a profile… lets you type in its channels.
Press + Scene to start from a preset look. Program lights lets you set colour, brightness, position, zoom, gobo and effects on any light while you watch.
When you're ready, pick a song and press Follow the show. The automatic lights follow the song's sections, and your own scenes fire where you've put them.
Before Sunday, you can run the whole setlist on the 3D stage without touching the real lights.

body.alt: The Lighting tab: the stage in 3D above the presets

articles.title: Slides, lyrics and the band's screen
articles.summary: Lyrics on a background, slides from the designer, scripture in seconds and a confidence monitor for the band.

items: Lyrics come from each song and follow the track as it plays. Under Lyrics, pick a background for the whole set, one song, or one part of a song. It crossfades when it changes.

The confidence monitor shows the band the current lines in yellow and the next lines in white, with chords, a clock and the time left. You can change what it shows in Settings → Confidence monitor on the lyrics computer.
Make slides in the designer with text, pictures, video and shapes, or import pictures, PDFs and PowerPoint files. Show mode puts Preview and Live side by side.
For scripture, type something like "John 3:16" or "Ps 23:1-4". It turns into slides and a lower third for the stream. King James, World English, American Standard and Reina-Valera 1909 are built in.
The video manager decides what each screen shows: lyrics, slides, a camera or the stream.

body.alt: Central Control's Slides tab with Preview and Live

articles.title: The stream and automatic shorts
articles.summary: Stream the service, record it, and let the built-in AI make short clips for social media.

items: Give one computer the Stream mix job on the Devices tab. Its Video tab sends the service to your stream destinations (RTMP or SRT) with a mix of its own.
Record the service with the record button on the Mix tab, or set it to start recording by itself.
Once a recording is 10 minutes or longer, Shorts finds the songs and the sermon and makes vertical clips with captions and draft titles.
Look through them on the Shorts tab of the main admin's computer. You can play, trim, fix captions, approve or delete each one.

Connect YouTube, Facebook, Instagram and TikTok in Shorts → Settings and approved clips post on the schedule you set, each with a link to the full stream. You can also download a clip and post it yourself.

body.text: How many shorts it makes, how long they are, and whether it also posts the whole worship set and the whole sermon as their own videos are all set in Shorts → Settings. It learns from what you approve and post, so the first few weeks are the roughest.

articles.title: Central Production basics
articles.summary: Make a track, a pad, an instrument or a plugin, and use it in your other apps.

body.text: Central Production is the studio I use to make the sounds that come with Central. It's free, and it opens the same projects on your computer and in the browser.

items: Open Central Production (the app, or /production/ on this website) and sign in so your projects are saved to your account.
File → New project asks what you're making: a track, loop, sample, pad, instrument, plugin or pedal board. The project opens set up for that.
In Settings → Audio, pick your audio interface and which input each track records from. Measure the delay there once so your recordings line up.
Record with a count-in, punch in and out, or loop takes. The mixer has sends, buses and automation, and the piano roll can quantize and humanize.
Export a WAV, an MP3 or the stems. Install into my apps puts what you made into Central Control and Central Usage on this computer, and Publish sends it to Make & sell or Central Tracks.

body.text: If you have a sound plan, the better sounds show up inside Central Production too.

articles.title: VST3 and CLAP plugins in Central Production
articles.summary: Put your own plugins on a track, play a keyboard through them and export with their automation.

items: Open the mixer, press + Effect on a track, choose Your VST3 / CLAP plugins…, then pick the plugin. The first time, it looks through this computer for your plugins.
Press play. The track plays through its plugins, lined up with the other tracks. Turn a knob in the panel, or press Open its window to use the plugin's own screen.

Settings → Audio → Plugin response sets how quickly you hear a knob change while the song plays. Balanced is right for most computers. If yours is fast, try Fast. If the sound breaks up, go to Safe. If the computer falls behind, it gives the plugins more time by itself and tells you.

Play a MIDI keyboard on an instrument track and you'll hear its plugins on every note. Settings → Audio → Keyboard through plugins has two choices. Lowest delay sends the SoundFont sound and the plugins straight to your sound card, with only a few milliseconds of delay, but leaves out the track's other effects. Through the whole track includes everything on the track and adds about 10 to 20 ms.
To automate a plugin knob, open the track's automation lanes with A. Exports, stems and freezing all keep the automation.
On a slower computer, right-click the track's name and choose Freeze. It plays from a rendered copy and frees up the computer. Change anything on the track and it plays live again.

body.text: VST3 and CLAP plugins play in the Central Production and Central Usage apps on Mac, Windows and Linux. The website version plays Central FX plugins, including ones you've built yourself, and plays a track you froze in the app.

articles.title: Delays that stay in time with the song
articles.summary: Make a delay follow the song's tempo on a note you pick, or give it its own time.

body.text: Every delay in the apps has a Sync to tempo switch. Turn it on and pick a note, like a quarter, a dotted eighth or an eighth triplet. The repeats land on that note at the song's tempo, and they follow when the next song is faster or slower. Turn it off and the delay keeps whatever time you set in milliseconds.
Where to find it depends on where the delay is:

items: On a pedal board (the Central Pedal, Central Control or Central Usage), tap the delay pedal, turn on Sync to tempo and pick the note.
For tracks, pads and buses on the Central Pedal, open FX and pick the note under Delay. With Central Plugins you can turn Sync to tempo off and type a time in milliseconds instead.
Central Control's shared delay is under Mix → Reverb & delay. Pick a note, or Free (ms). A delay you've put on a channel has its own Sync to tempo switch.
In Central Production and the Central Usage Studio, the Delay effect has Sync to tempo, a note and a time. It follows tempo changes inside a song, and exports keep them.

The Central FX delays (Delay, Tape Echo and Ping-Pong) have Sync to tempo with a note. The Dotted Eighth Delay follows the tempo on its own. Switch off Sync to song tempo if you'd rather set its tempo by hand.
If you're building your own plugin, select a Delay block and pick a note under Sync to tempo. The plugin gets a Tempo knob, and the apps set it to the song's tempo for you.

body.text: Delays you saved before this change sound the same as they did. A few third-party pedals don't have a time knob the apps can set exactly: the multiband delays, Zyn Echo, mda Delay, the Tape Delay, Delayorama and TAP Echo. Set those by ear.

articles.title: Keys, devices and renewals
articles.summary: Where your keys are, moving a key to a new computer, and what renewing does.

items: Every key you or your church owns is under Account → My products, with the devices it's on and a Copy button. We emailed them to you too.
Got a new computer? Press Release next to the old one, then type the key into the app on the new one.
A sound plan comes as one package key. It works on three of your devices at once, as long as each is a different app, for example Central Usage, Central Control and your pedal.

Central Control and Central Usage keys come with ten releases of updates from when you buy them. Buy at 10.4 and you get every update up to 11.4. Renewing costs $20 and adds ten more. If you don't renew, the apps keep working. They just stop updating.
Sound plans renew every year and Central Tracks Unlimited every month. You can cancel either one from Account → Billing.

articles.title: No sound? Start here
articles.summary: Work through these in order. Most problems turn up in the first two.

items: On the pedal, open Settings → Sound → Test sound and press 1. The pedal plays a tone, listens along the way and tells you underneath where the sound stopped. It fixes what it can, so press 1 again afterwards.
Still nothing? Press Play on each sound card. That plays a tone straight out of each card, skipping the app. If that's silent too, it's the cable, the headphones or whatever they're plugged into.
If the headphone jack crackles and you can't hear the music, open Settings → Sound → Output device and set Headphone jack buffer to Biggest.
Using a USB interface? Plug it in before you turn the pedal on, and check it's listed under Settings → Sound → Output device. Its outputs come after the jack, and after the DAC board if you have one.
If you're still stuck, contact support from Help on this website or from Settings → About & power on the pedal. Write down what Test sound said. It tells me exactly where to look.

articles.title: Update failed, "can't reach the website" or the pedal is offline
articles.summary: What each message means and what to do about it.

body.text: An update failed

The apps download their updates from GitHub. On Linux, an update waits while the computer installs its own updates, then tries again. If it still can't, it tells you why. Settings → Software updates has a Try again button, and you can always download the newest version from Downloads on this website.
"Couldn't reach the Motion Audio website"

Check the device is online. The status page (/status) shows whether sign-in, downloads and payments are working right now. Your apps keep working without the internet and check your key again once they're back online.
The pedal shows as offline

items: Make sure the pedal is on and on the same Wi-Fi as your computer. You can check under Settings → Network & devices on the pedal.
Some church networks keep devices from seeing each other. Ask whoever runs your network to allow it, or plug in a network cable.
In Central Control or Central Pedal Control, type the pedal's address into Connect. The address is under Settings → About & power on the pedal.
